title: Blocking I/O, Event Loops, and Async/Await
instructions: Answer from the lesson. For short-answer and practical items, equivalent technically correct wording/code earns credit.

questions.prompt: What is the main benefit of async I/O?

options.text: Lets tasks make progress while waiting for I/O

questions.explanation: Async I/O helps overlap waiting time among concurrent tasks.

questions.prompt: Does an HTTP 404 response normally make JavaScript fetch reject automatically?
questions.explanation: Fetch resolves for HTTP error statuses; callers should inspect `ok`/status.

questions.expected_answer: Async I/O can be concurrent without CPU parallelism.

questions.prompt: Why might adding `async` to a CPU-bound loop not speed it up?
questions.expected_answer: CPU-bound work may need processes, threads/native code, or algorithmic optimization.

questions.prompt: What should a Node.js fetch example check before parsing JSON?
questions.expected_answer: Valid answer handles HTTP status separately from network exceptions.
